live.instructions: Use this server to query and modify Blynk IoT platform entities for the authenticated organization. It supports searching devices and templates, retrieving their details, and creating or updating platform entities. Use this server when a request requires live Blynk platform data or platform-side changes. Do not use it for general explanations, documentation, or hypothetical guidance.

tools.name: detect_device_data_gaps
tools.description: Detect missing-data periods (gaps) for a datastream across a device set over a time window. Useful for fault localization and monitoring reporting health. Each device's expected reporting cadence is auto-detected as the median interval between its consecutive readings, so devices that report every few seconds and devices that report once a day are both handled; pass 'expectedPeriodSeconds' to override it. A gap is a spacing between two consecutive readings that exceeds the expected cadence times 'gapMultiplier' (default 2). Returns gap clusters (deviceId, startTs, endTs, durationS) ordered by descending duration, the total gap count, the number of affected devices, and a 'truncated' flag when the list was capped. Interpret the results with these limits in mind: (1) only gaps BETWEEN two readings are detected — silence before the first or after the last reading in the window is NOT reported, so a device that went fully silent (or has not reported recently) shows no gap here; check its last-seen time separately to catch that. (2) durationS is the spacing between the two surrounding readings, so it can overstate the actual no-data time by up to one reporting interval. (3) the cadence is the median interval, so a device whose outages dominate the window can under-report gaps (its 'normal' cadence looks large); set 'expectedPeriodSeconds' when you know the intended interval. (4) when 'truncated' is true the results are capped to the longest gaps, so gapCountTotal and affectedDevices then count only the returned gaps, not the true totals. The time range must not span more than 100000 buckets for the chosen granularity, and the resolved device set must not exceed 1000 devices (at most 100 when listed explicitly via 'deviceUris'); narrow the range, use a coarser granularity, or narrow the segment if it does.

gapMultiplier.description: A gap is flagged when the spacing between two consecutive reported buckets exceeds the expected period times this factor. Must be greater than 1. Defaults to 2 (i.e. at least one full expected reporting interval was missed).

tools.name: detect_device_data_gaps
tools.description: Detect missing-data periods (gaps) for a datastream across a device set over a time window. Useful for fault localization and monitoring reporting health. Each device's expected reporting cadence is auto-detected as the median interval between its consecutive readings, so devices that report every few seconds and devices that report once a day are both handled; pass 'expectedPeriodSeconds' to override it. A gap is a spacing between two consecutive readings that exceeds the expected cadence times 'gapMultiplier' (default 2). Returns gap clusters (deviceId, startTs, endTs, durationS) ordered by descending duration, the total gap count, the number of affected devices, and a 'truncated' flag when the list was capped. Interpret the results with these limits in mind: (1) only gaps BETWEEN two readings are detected — silence before the first or after the last reading in the window is NOT reported, so a device that went fully silent (or has not reported recently) shows no gap here; check its last-seen time separately to catch that. (2) durationS is the spacing between the two surrounding readings, so it can overstate the actual no-data time by up to one reporting interval. (3) the cadence is the median interval, so a device whose outages dominate the window can under-report gaps (its 'normal' cadence looks large); set 'expectedPeriodSeconds' when you know the intended interval. (4) when 'truncated' is true the results are capped to the longest gaps, so gapCountTotal and affectedDevices then count only the returned gaps, not the true totals. The time range must not span more than 100000 buckets for the chosen granularity, and the resolved device set must not exceed 1000 devices (at most 100 when listed explicitly via 'deviceUris'); narrow the range, use a coarser granularity, or narrow the segment if it does.

gapMultiplier.description: A gap is flagged when the spacing between two consecutive reported buckets exceeds the expected period times this factor. Must be greater than 1. Defaults to 2 (i.e. at least one full expected reporting interval was missed).

deviceUris.description: Explicit list of device URIs (e.g. 'device://12345') to scan. Use this when you already know the specific devices and don't need a segment query. Provide exactly one of 'segmentId', 'segment' or 'deviceUris'. Maximum 100 URIs.

segment.description: Ad-hoc device segment definition. Mutually exclusive with 'segmentId' and 'deviceUris' — provide exactly one of the three selectors on the parent tool.
